subject: Request: Uptime credit calculation for DNS downstream impact (Medlink Health)
messages:
From: Emma Clark <emma.clark@medlink.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 18:22:00 -0800
Subject: Partial degradation Nov 3 - request for credit calculation

Hi Jasmine,

We observed a sustained spike in failed requests to the Redwood API between 13:45-14:30 UTC on Nov 3. Our telemetry shows ~20% of requests during that 45-minute window resulted in DNS resolution timeouts before they reached Redwood (we see NX/timeout at the edge). We opened a ticket with our DNS provider (FastDNS ticket #78923) who confirms a chain-of-resolvers issue during the same window.

Because this reduced our request success rate and impacted customer-facing flows, we'd like Redwood to perform an uptime calculation and provide the amount of SLA credit Medlink is eligible for under our contract (Section 4.2.2). I've attached a small sample of our logs (medlink_error_sample.log) and the FastDNS acknowledgement (fastdns_ticket_78923.pdf).

Questions:
- How does Redwood treat third-party DNS chain failures when attributing availability?
- If some percentage of requests never reach Redwood due to DNS failure, are those counted as Redwood downtime or excluded as third-party outages?

Appreciate a quick confirmation of next steps — we need the calculation to complete our internal post-mortem.

Thanks,
Emma Clark
Senior Platform Engineer
Medlink Health

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Emma Clark <emma.clark@medlink.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 19:40:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Partial degradation Nov 3 - request for credit calculation

Hi Emma — thanks for the report and attachments, and sorry for the disruption. I'm looping in Marissa (AM) and Ben (SRE lead) to ensure we track appropriately.

Two quick clarifying asks for our audit:
1) Can you confirm whether the failed requests you saw returned HTTP errors from our edge (4xx/5xx) or whether they timed out during DNS resolution and never reached us?
2) Do you have an ingress timeline mapping from your clients showing retries vs initial failures?

High-level on our side: Redwood's standard uptime calculations exclude outages clearly attributable to upstream providers when the requests never reach Redwood's edge (per the SLA appendix). However, partial degradations (when some requests reach Redwood but throughput/latency is impacted) are handled by pro-rating the affected window. We need to correlate your ingress telemetry with our edge logs to decide whether this is an upstream exclusion or a partial degradation on our ledger.

I've created a support ticket SUP-4579 and attached it to this thread; we'll pull edge logs for 13:30-14:45 UTC to correlate.

-Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Emma Clark <emma.clark@medlink.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:15:37 -0800
Subject: Re: Partial degradation Nov 3 - request for credit calculation

Jasmine — thanks for the quick reply.

To confirm: the majority of the failures show DNS timeouts (no HTTP response observed) — our client logs indicate retries but clients typically gave up after two attempts. I've attached a filtered excerpt (medlink_error_sample.log) showing the resolver timeouts and the FastDNS PDF. We don't see 4xx/5xx from Redwood in our logs.

We can share a fuller ingress trace if needed; we've redacted PII but can provide traces keyed by request IDs. Please let us know what you need for a formal exclusion vs partial-degrade determination.

Best,
Emma

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Emma Clark <emma.clark@medlink.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 16:00:05 -0800
Subject: Re: Partial degradation Nov 3 - request for credit calculation

Emma — thank you for the extra detail and the artifacts. I've reviewed Medlink's sample and our preliminary edge logs for SUP-4579. Summary to be clear:

- Redwood edge telemetry shows normal capacity and no internal 5xx spike during 13:30–14:45 UTC.
- A small fraction (~3%) of requests that reached our network returned 5xx during a short overlapping window (13:52–13:54 UTC) due to transient upstream health checks, but the bulk of the error tail is consistent with DNS resolution failures before connection.

Per Section 5 of our SLA, outages attributable to upstream resolvers that prevent requests from reaching Redwood are treated as third-party exclusions and are not assigned as Redwood downtime. However, for partial degradations (where a proportion of customers experienced reduced success because of client-side retries that reached Redwood but were rate-limited) we pro-rate credit by the fraction of user-facing successful calls impacted.

Given the data:
- We will exclude the window where requests clearly never reached our edge (13:45–14:30 UTC) from Redwood's downtime accounting.
- We will apply a partial degradation credit to the short overlapping internal 13:52–13:54 UTC period where our logs show 5xx returns (this maps to ~3% of your measured traffic).

Provisional calculation (illustrative): 3% impact over a 2-minute window within a 30-day month results in a fractional credit of ~0.00014 of monthly invoice. That converts to roughly a 10% credit on the invoice slice attributable to affected API calls during the window — we will finalize after you confirm acceptance of this method.

Next steps: if you'd like us to proceed with a formal re-evaluation and credit issuance, reply with approval and we will open a billing claim referencing SUP-4579 and HubSpot ML-7890. I can also schedule a short call if you prefer to walk through the math.

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0123
